answers.confusion_update_granularity: sampled token, then aggregated into layer/head/bucket rows.
answers.raw_pattern_mse_retention: raw/pattern MSE retained as scalar summaries, not as per-candidate CSV columns.
answers.tp_tn_fp_fn_definition: token-level gate-vs-oracle confusion over sampled prefill tokens.

findings.evidence: oracle = pattern_mse_vec < raw_mse_vec; gate is the current mask.
findings.interpretation: Positive class means pattern wins over raw; gate acceptance is predicted positive.

findings.evidence: tp = gate & oracle; tn = ~gate & ~oracle; fp = gate & ~oracle; fn = ~gate & oracle.
findings.interpretation: TP/TN/FP/FN are token-level confusion counts, not per-sample labels.
Confusion counters are accumulated directly into the collector.

findings.evidence: raw_mse, pattern_candidate_mse, actual_selected_path_mse, relative_candidate_benefit are recorded as scalars.
findings.interpretation: The raw/pattern MSE signals exist in raw observer output, but not in the summary confusion CSV.

findings.evidence: sample record contains gate_current, gate_oracle, rho, false_positive_penalty, false_negative_opportunity.
findings.interpretation: Candidate-level sweep fields exist only in sample records, not in v_gate_confusion.csv.

findings.evidence: confusion_store accumulates counters from observer payloads.
findings.interpretation: CSV rows are built from complete confusion counters, not from truncated sample records.

findings.evidence: v_gate_rows are generated from aggregated confusion_store totals.
findings.interpretation: The published CSV reflects aggregate counts at task/layer/head/bucket granularity.
